summary: Built 1930 as a 94-foot tower near Garrison, phoned in 1936, vandalized in 1970, now listed as gone; no removal date found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source found gives a removal date.

events.note: 94-foot tower of a new type completed
Board approved poles and telephone line from Brainerd to the tower
23-mile telephone line to the Brainerd district ranger completed
June vandalism: windows broken, fire finder ruined, map taken, stool smashed
August vandalism: trap door and 20 plate-glass windows smashed

evidence.supports: listed as gone, Crow Wing County
evidence.quote: Borden Lake Crow Wing 46.27874 -93.85757 Tower Gone

evidence.supports: dated 2 May 1930: completed 1930, 94-foot tower, manned on completion
evidence.quote: Adding protection to the woods from forest fires, a 94-foot tower of the new type stands completed today and manned at Borden Lake.

evidence.supports: sixth of its type in the district, under E.H. Rhodes
evidence.quote: The tower is the sixth of the new type in use in this district under supervision of E.H. Rhodes, district forest ranger.
The tower is located near Garrison.

evidence.supports: dated 10 Sept 1935: board approved poles and telephone wire along county roads
evidence.quote: The board approved a request of the State Forestry department for the right to set up poles and string telephone line along the right of way of county roads.

evidence.supports: line to run from Brainerd to the tower
evidence.quote: The line will run from Brainerd to the Borden lake lookout tower, the petition said.

evidence.supports: dated 2 Apr 1936: 23 miles of metallic telephone line built to the Brainerd district ranger
evidence.quote: Twenty-three miles of metallic telephone line was built connecting the Borden Lake fire tower with the forest service district ranger at Brainerd.

evidence.supports: dated 26 June 1970: vandals damaged the tower
evidence.quote: Vandals damaged the Borden lake forestry tower recently, according to forestry officials and the sheriff's office here.

evidence.supports: dated 26 June 1970: damage list (five windows, fire finder, map, stool)
evidence.quote: Officials said that five windows were broken, the fire finder ruined, a map taken and a stool smashed.

evidence.supports: dated 21 Aug 1970: trap door and 20 plate-glass windows smashed
evidence.quote: Someone smashed a trap door and 20 plate glass windows at the Borden Lake fire tower.

sources.title: Borden Lake, Forest Lookouts (transcribed Brainerd Daily Dispatch items)

notes_for_editor: Removal date and cause unknown; no source here gives them. The 1931 item about a phone rented for 'the fire tower on Warren's hill' is not tied to Borden Lake, so it is left out. The 1930-1970 items are transcriptions of Brainerd Daily Dispatch articles on the Central US Lookouts page; the originals were not checked. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the story's dates (2 May 1930, 10 Sept 1935, 2 Apr 1936, 26 June 1970, 21 Aug 1970) are the dates printed on that page. The 94-foot figure stays in the story as the page prints it, but height_m was removed from facts because the page does not say the height is to the cab floor, which is what the field means. The story's sentence about the June damage now attributes the list to officials, as the transcription does. Record coordinates sit about 3 km from the Wikipedia lake coordinates (46.305, -93.854); not treated as a conflict. Suggested checks: Brainerd Daily Dispatch archive, MN DNR forestry records, Crow Wing County Historical Society.
